rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO): annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement:
In RSO units, rent may be raised once every 12 months by the allowable percentage published by LAHD. That percentage was 3% for July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026.

Add-ons:
- From February 2, 2026, no extra percentage for utilities and no 10% add-on for an added dependent.
- A 10% increase for an additional non-dependent tenant is still allowed if taken within 60 days of the landlord learning of that tenant.

Increases above the allowable percentage need LAHD approval. The approval programs are capital improvement, primary renovation, seismic retrofit, rehabilitation, and just and reasonable rent increase.

Rent may go to market rate after any of these:
- a voluntary move-out
- eviction for nonpayment, lease violation, Tenant Habitability Plan noncompliance or a City Attorney order
- a Tenant Buyout Agreement

Rent increases were prohibited from March 30, 2020 through January 31, 2024.

Landlords may pass through these surcharges, separate from rent, only after registering the units and giving written notice:
- RSO registration surcharge: $1.61 per month
- SCEP surcharge: $2.83 per month
- smoke or CO detector surcharge: $3.00

Per LAHD, state law requires 30 days' written notice for increases under 10%.
rules.key_value: One increase per 12 months at the LAHD allowable percentage. 3% for 7/1/2025-6/30/2026; the figure for 7/1/2026 onward is not in the documents. No utility or dependent add-on from 2026-02-02. +10% for an additional non-dependent tenant, within 60 days. Surcharges: RSO $1.61/mo, SCEP $2.83/mo, smoke detector $3.00.

unverifiable_exemptions: Luxury exemption (landlord must establish the monthly rent charged on or before May 31, 1978)
Condominium or townhome tenancy commenced after December 31, 1995 (rent not regulated)
coverage.summary:
Covers rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28. Included unit types:
- apartments and duplexes
- two or more single-family dwellings on one parcel
- hotel, motel, rooming-house or boarding-house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days
- residential units attached to commercial buildings
- ADUs and JADUs
- mobile homes and RVs in mobile home parks

Condominiums and townhomes are covered, but their rent is not regulated for tenancies commenced after December 31, 1995. RSO units are excluded from the state cap (Civ. Code § 1947.12), so the RSO governs them.
coverage.other_conditions: Rent may reset to market after a voluntary vacancy, certain at-fault evictions or a buyout agreement. SCEP and RSO surcharges are collectible only after registration and written notice.

rules.exemptions: Luxury exemption on application; temporary exemptions filed with LAHD; condominium and townhome tenancies commenced after 12/31/1995 are not rent-regulated.
rules.effective_date_note: 2026-02-02 is the LAHD-published date the utility and dependent add-ons ended, which is the current version of the increase rules. The RSO's original effective date is not stated. The 3% rate applied July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026. Increases were prohibited March 30, 2020 through January 31, 2024.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO eviction controls, notice filing and no-fault relocation assistance
rules.requirement:
RSO tenancies may be terminated only for listed causes.

At-fault causes:
- nonpayment
- uncured lease violation
- nuisance or damage
- illegal use
- refusal to renew a similar agreement
- denial of reasonable access
- unapproved subtenant

Per LAHD, from March 27, 2023 a nonpayment eviction requires the tenant to owe more than the Fair Market Rent for the unit's bedroom size.

No-fault causes:
- owner or relative move-in
- resident manager, only if required by law, an affordable-housing covenant or a regulatory agreement
- demolition or removal from rental use (Ellis Act, LAMC 151.22-151.28)
- government order to vacate
- HUD sale
- residential hotel conversion
- conversion to affordable housing

For a no-fault eviction, the landlord must:
- file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving any termination notice
- give 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions need 120 days or up to a 1-year extension)
- make relocation assistance available within 15 days of service, or place it in escrow within that period

Relocation is paid per unit, split pro rata, at the higher amount if more than one applies. Accumulated rent may be offset, except for government vacate orders.

Every termination notice must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service.

From August 20, 2025, the Notice of Right to Counsel must be posted, given at the start of the tenancy, and attached to any eviction notice.

rules.exemptions: No relocation is owed when replacing one resident manager with another, or for an eviction forced by natural-disaster hazards not caused by the landlord's negligence. Rent offset is not allowed for government vacate orders or unpermitted-dwelling orders.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement:
Landlords of covered non-RSO units may not terminate a tenancy without just cause.

At-fault causes:
- nonpayment (from March 27, 2023, only if the tenant owes more than the Fair Market Rent for the bedroom size)
- uncured lease violation
- nuisance or damage
- illegal use
- refusal to renew a similar agreement
- denial of reasonable access
- unapproved subtenant
At-fault evictions carry no relocation.

No-fault causes:
- owner or immediate family move-in
- resident manager, when required by law, covenant or regulatory agreement
- demolition, permanent removal or conversion to non-residential use
- government vacate order
- HUD sale
- residential hotel conversion or demolition
- conversion to affordable housing

For a no-fault eviction, the landlord must:
- file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice
- pay relocation assistance at the RSO Chart A amounts within 15 days of service, or into escrow within that period
For a single-family dwelling owned by a natural person with no more than four units plus a separate-lot single-family home in the City, relocation is one month's rent, as a payment or a credit. Accumulated rent may be offset, except for government vacate or unpermitted-dwelling orders.

Eviction notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service.

Other duties:
- register properties annually
- post the Notice of Right to Counsel from August 20, 2025, and give it at the start of the tenancy and with any eviction notice
- give the Notice of Renters' Protections to tenancies beginning or renewing on or after January 27, 2023

- Qualified: $23,150 / $27,400
- Single-family dwelling owned by a qualifying natural person: one month's rent
Other terms:
- relocation paid within 15 days
- notice filed with LAHD within 3 business days
- nonpayment eviction only above FMR (from 3/27/2023)
- Right to Counsel notice from 8/20/2025
- Renters' Protections notice from 1/27/2023

coverage.summary:
Covers most residential property in the City of Los Angeles that is not regulated by the RSO, complementing the RSO's October 1, 1978 cutoff. It can apply to buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and to a property with only one single-family dwelling.

The tenant must have lived in the unit at least six months, or the original lease must have expired, whichever comes first.

Covered units follow the JCO rather than Civ. Code § 1946.2. Rent increases on JCO units are governed by state AB 1482, not the JCO.

rules.title: Los Angeles Resident Protections Ordinance (RPO): relocation and occupant protections for demolition for new construction
rules.requirement:
This applies when a Protected Unit is demolished for new construction within 5 years after the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict is filed. All RSO units are Protected Units.

The owner must:
- file with LAHD
- serve notice and file a copy within 3 business days
- pay the RSO or JCO relocation amounts within 15 days

Lower-income households (at or below 80% AMI) get enhanced relocation. The owner pays the higher of the state Housing Crisis Act or City amounts and chooses one of three options:
- Option 1: standardized Chart B payment through the City's Relocation Consultant
- Option 2: an approved comparable replacement unit plus Chart A amounts
- Option 3: individualized relocation under an approved plan

Occupant protections:
- right to relocation
- right to remain up to 6 months before construction, including a 6-month notice
- right to return if demolition does not proceed
- right of first refusal for some tenants
- tenant notification

Noncompliance may bring penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.

rules.title: Los Angeles relocation assistance for demolition or conversion (LAMC 47.06 and 47.07)
rules.requirement:
A landlord who demolishes a rental property, or converts it to condominiums, stock cooperatives, community apartment projects, hotels or commercial uses, must pay relocation assistance. This applies whether or not the property is under the RSO or JCO.

Once the City has approved a tentative parcel or tract map for a condominium conversion, the tenant may elect to relocate without receiving a termination notice. The landlord still owes relocation assistance.

coverage.summary: Rental property in the City being demolished or converted to condominiums, cooperatives, community apartment projects, hotels or commercial use, regardless of RSO/JCO coverage.
coverage.other_conditions: Triggered only by demolition or conversion.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO security deposit interest
rules.requirement:
Landlords of RSO units must pay tenants interest on security deposits. Interest accrues monthly from November 1, 1990, at a rate the City sets each year.

The landlord chooses to pay the accrued interest either directly or as a credit against rent, and must notify the tenant of that choice in writing. Payment is made monthly or yearly. Waiting until the end of the tenancy does not comply.
rules.key_value: Interest accrues monthly from 11/1/1990 and is paid monthly or yearly, by direct payment or rent credit, with written notice of the method. Rate set annually by the City: 4.320% for calendar 2025 (per AAGLA); no 2026 rate in the documents.

coverage.summary: Rental units subject to the Los Angeles RSO. Operates alongside the state deposit cap and return rules (Civ. Code § 1950.5).
coverage.construction_date_basis: RSO coverage (first built on or before Oct. 1, 1978, plus replacement units)
coverage.other_conditions: Property must be subject to the RSO.

rules.effective_date_note: November 1, 1990 is the date interest began accruing, per the LAMC text quoted by AAGLA.
citation_aliases: L.A. Mun. Code ch. XV, art. 1
rules.review_note: The substantive code text comes only from a secondary article quoting LAMC § 151.06.02. The rate table was last updated 5/21/25. The 2026 rate is not given and should be confirmed with LAHD; the 2025 figure of 4.320% is far above prior years and should also be verified.
rules.source_notes: The official LAHD RSO Overview (D041) lists security deposit interest as an RSO subject. The rule text and rates come from the AAGLA article (DX12; the same URL is listed as link-only D044).

also_supported_by.quoted_span: Interest shall begin accruing on November 1, 1990, on a monthly basis. A tenant shall be given the unpaid accrued interest in the form of either a direct payment or a credit against the tenant’s rent. The landlord shall choose between these two methods of payment and notify the tenant in writing of his or her choice. The landlord may elect to pay the accrued interest on a monthly or yearly basis.
